description: This public GitHub repository contains code for generating long European hourly solar, onshore wind, offshore wind and electricity-demand profiles from ERA5 weather predictors and measured ENTSO-E records. Its README identifies the published Zenodo output and lists country cleaning notebooks, ERA5 preparation, machine-learning scripts and model-evaluation steps. GitHub licence metadata and the README state MIT for the code; the output data are separately CC BY 4.0. A power-system modeller can generate or adapt weather-year profiles before capacity-planning runs with model-pypsa. A caveat is that training is stochastic, so the README says reruns reproduce model errors within neural-network variation, not byte-for-byte. Current ERA5 reprocessing and source-platform terms can also alter an input download. Some countries lack sufficient measured data, and Kosovo uses a Serbian holiday calendar as a proxy. I read own repository metadata and README but did not download ERA5 data, install dependencies, retrain networks or compare generated values with the Zenodo archive.
